comments.body:
## Measured: the liveness rule is inconsistent across relations, and BOTH of P6's remedies are refused

Filing this ticket produced the comparison for free. Against closed tickets, on the same
store, in the same minute:

| Attempted link | Endpoint that is closed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `0461 --depends_on--> 2041` | target | **REFUSED** — "target ticket is closed" |
| `2041 --blocks--> 0461` | source | **REFUSED** — "source ticket is closed. Reopen it first with: `ticket transition 2041 closed open`" |
| `1544 --relates_to--> 868c` | target | ok |
| `1544 --relates_to--> 266e` | target | ok |
| `1544 --discovered_from--> 0461` | — (open) | ok |

Two things this settles.

**1. The link layer does not apply one liveness rule.** `relates_to` accepts a closed target
without complaint; `depends_on` refuses one. Nothing about the two relations justifies the
split — if anything the case for allowing it is stronger for `depends_on`, which records a
real ordering between two pieces of work, than for `relates_to`, which records only that
someone found them relevant to each other. So the defect is not "`depends_on` forgot to allow
closed targets"; it is that endpoint liveness is decided relation by relation with no stated
rule, so each relation's behaviour is whatever its own code path happened to do. `868c` is the
same thing on `supersedes`/closed-source. That is 3 relations with 3 answers and no table.

**2. `P6`'s constructive remedies are both unavailable, not just one.** The criterion offers
three: add `depends_on`, ensure the cited ticket `blocks` this one, or remove the citation.
The first two are the same edge seen from either end, and both are refused the moment the
upstream ticket merges. Only "remove the citation" survives — discarding accurate provenance
to satisfy a tool. So a plan that builds on MERGED work can never ground its citation to the
ticket that delivered that work, which is the case where the citation is most certainly
correct.

The `blocks` refusal also suggests its own remedy: "Reopen it first." Reopening a merged,
verified, closed ticket in order to record that later work depends on it would corrupt the
tracker's record of what is done to work around a link-layer rule.

## Not a blocker for 0461

`P6` is advisory (`decision: advisory`, `severity: minor`, `impact: 0.4`), so 0461's review is
not held by this. The cost is narrower and worth stating precisely: the citation to the ticket
that delivered the code 0461 builds on is "grounded as normal (fails closed)" instead of as a
verified prerequisite. The review still runs; it just cannot use the strongest evidence
available to it.

## Unverified

Whether `duplicates` and `caused_by` enforce liveness, and on which endpoint, has not been
measured. The fix's table needs all 6 relations, not the 4 observed here.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar link 0461-09ce-4850-42a7 2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9 depends_on` was refused with
`Error: cannot create depends_on link — target ticket '2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9' is closed`.
2041 is closed because it MERGED, and 0461 builds on the work it delivered. A `depends_on`
edge records "this work rests on that work"; it is more certain once the target has landed,
not less. The refusal makes the edge expressible only while the dependency is unproven.

The plan-review `P6` citation check (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_citation.py:128-148`,
`_edge_verified`) asks for exactly this edge: a `[rebar:<id>]` citation is a verified upstream
prerequisite only when `P depends_on C` or `C blocks P`. Once C closes, `P depends_on C` is
refused by this guard and `C blocks P` is refused by the closed-source guard, so a plan that
builds on merged work can never ground its citation to the ticket that delivered it.

## Root cause (reproduced on origin/main 9233a47ac6a)

`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:45-62` `_refuse_closed_endpoints` holds two independent rules:
a closed SOURCE is refused for every relation except those in
`_CLOSED_SOURCE_RELATIONS_ALLOWED = {"supersedes"}` (`_links.py:42`, from
`unpaid-sanctified-aardvark`), and a closed TARGET is refused by a hard-coded
`relation == "depends_on"` branch (`_links.py:61-62`). The closed-target branch came verbatim
from the bash engine in the DSO extraction `b534f47a7f9` (`ticket-link.sh:180-189`, test
"Test 10") with no stated rationale.

Scratch reproduction in a fresh store, open source to closed target, one fresh pair per
relation: `blocks`, `relates_to`, `duplicates`, `supersedes`, `discovered_from` are accepted;
`depends_on` is refused with the closed-target error; `caused_by` is refused by its separate
commit-reference rule (`_commands/link_revert.py`), which is unrelated to liveness. So the
closed-target rule singles out `depends_on` alone, while `blocks` — the other blocking
relation (`graph/_relations.py` `_BLOCKING_RELATIONS`) — accepts a closed target.

Readiness does not need the guard: with the guard bypassed (writing the LINK event directly),
`rebar.ready()` still returns the source whose only `depends_on` target is closed, and
`tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_unresolved_blocker.py:55`
(`test_depends_on_resolvable_closed_target_is_ready`) already pins that a closed `depends_on`
target counts as satisfied. P6 (`det_citation._declares_depends_on`) reads the edge without
checking the target's status, so once the edge exists P6 accepts it.

## Approach

Replace the two ad-hoc rules with ONE per-relation endpoint-liveness table in
`src/rebar/graph/_links.py`, consulted by `_refuse_closed_endpoints` for both endpoints:

- `_ENDPOINT_LIVENESS: dict[str, tuple[bool, bool]]` maps every relation in
  `CANONICAL_RELATIONS` to `(source_must_be_open, target_must_be_open)`.
- Source column: `True` for every relation except `supersedes` (unchanged behaviour; the
  `blocks` mirror stays refused per this ticket's out-of-scope note).
- Target column: `False` for every relation. This is the fix: `depends_on` joins the
  others in accepting a closed target, because a dependency on finished work is satisfied, not
  invalid, and `ready` already treats it that way.
- `_refuse_closed_endpoints` indexes the table directly (`_ENDPOINT_LIVENESS[relation]`, no
  default), so a relation added to `CANONICAL_RELATIONS` without a table row fails loudly
  instead of silently inheriting a rule. `_CLOSED_SOURCE_RELATIONS_ALLOWED` is removed
  (its only reference is `_links.py`; grep shows no other user).
- The closed-source error text keeps its `cannot create` / `is closed` wording, which the
  reconciler's `impossible_links._SIGNATURES` classifier matches.

Rejected: narrowing the `depends_on` branch to a second allow-set — that keeps 2 relations
each guessing independently, which AC4 rules out.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` — the liveness table and `_refuse_closed_endpoints`.
- `tests/unit/test_supersedes_closed_source.py` — invert
  `test_depends_on_still_refuses_a_closed_target` (it pinned the defect).
- `tests/unit/test_link_endpoint_liveness.py` (new) — per-relation pins, the P6 fixture
  test, and the `ready` check.
- `docs/ticket-model.md` — the closed-endpoint paragraph (`:146-149`) gains the target rule.

## Testing

Failing first, in `tests/unit/test_link_endpoint_liveness.py`, over a scratch store built
the same way as `tests/unit/test_supersedes_closed_source.py:25-39`:

- Happy path: `rebar.link(<open>, <closed>, "depends_on")` succeeds and
  `rebar.deps(<open>)` and the reduced `deps` of the source contain the edge (red before the fix).
- `ready`: the source with only a closed `depends_on` target is in `rebar.ready()`.
- P6: `p6_ac_quality(PlanContext(...))` over a fixture plan citing `[rebar:<closed>]`,
  with `state` reduced from the store and `tickets_root` set, reports
  `citation_gaps == 0` after the link; a control with no link reports `citation_gaps == 1`.
- Per relation x endpoint: for every relation in `CANONICAL_RELATIONS`, a closed target is
  accepted at `add_dependency`, and a closed source is refused unless the relation is
  `supersedes`; plus a test that the table's keys equal `CANONICAL_RELATIONS`.
- Edge: a closed `depends_on` target still runs the cycle guard (an existing reverse edge
  still raises `CyclicDependencyError`).

Then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the affected suites (`tests/unit/test_supersedes_closed_source.py`,
`tests/unit/test_link_endpoint_liveness.py`, `tests/scripts/graph/`, `tests/unit/plan_review/`,
`tests/unit/reconciler/`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar link <open> <closed> depends_on` succeeds, and `rebar deps <open>` (library `rebar.deps`) reports the edge — the ticket's original AC named `rebar ticket-deps`, which is not a subcommand; proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_link_endpoint_liveness.py -q`.
- [x] A closed `depends_on` target does NOT make the source unready: `rebar ready` still returns the source when its only unmet edge is a closed `depends_on` target; proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_link_endpoint_liveness.py -q`.
- [x] The plan-review `P6` criterion accepts a `depends_on` edge to a closed target as a VERIFIED upstream prerequisite, proved by a review over a fixture plan citing a closed ticket; proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_link_endpoint_liveness.py -q`.
- [x] The relation/endpoint liveness rules are stated in one place (`_ENDPOINT_LIVENESS` in `src/rebar/graph/_links.py`) that both `supersedes` and `depends_on` consult, rather than per-relation branches.
- [x] A test pins each relation's endpoint-liveness rule, so a future relation cannot silently inherit the wrong one; proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_link_endpoint_liveness.py -q`.
- [x] `make verify` passes.

## Out of scope

Changing what `blocks` means for a closed ticket (a closed source stays refused for `blocks`),
and any change to the disposition-close path that `unpaid-sanctified-aardvark` already covers.

file_impact.reason: single per-relation endpoint-liveness table; drop the depends_on closed-target refusal
invert the test that pinned the closed-target refusal
new per-relation liveness pins, ready check, and P6 fixture test
document the closed-target rule beside the closed-source rule
